vulnerabilities.description: Auth token obtained via getAccessTokenSilently() but never sent in API request headers. Token is fetched but discarded, breaking authentication chain. Backend cannot verify user identity or enforce ownership checks.
Auth token obtained via getAccessTokenSilently() but never included in fetch request headers. Token is retrieved then ignored, leaving request unauthenticated.
Auth token obtained but never added to fetch headers. FormData sent without Authorization header despite authenticated user context.
Content processed through ReactMarkdown without sanitization. If TERMS_OF_SERVICE is ever sourced from dynamic content, XSS is possible via markdown injection.
Auth token obtained but never used in fetch headers. Payment intent creation request sent without authentication.
Full error stack traces sent to window.logError without sanitization. If sent to external service, leaks application architecture and internal structure.
File size validation (25MB limit) is client-side only. Backend must also validate to prevent resource exhaustion.
TOS acceptance stored in localStorage. Backend should re-verify independently on each request rather than trusting client cache.
Payment amount logic depends on client state. Backend must recalculate price from documentType, never trust client-provided amounts.
Development-only skipPayment bypass could be exploited if NODE_ENV check fails. Remove this bypass in production.
Form inputs stored in state without sanitization. If rendered as HTML elsewhere, DOM-based XSS is possible.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Fix missing Authorization headers - tokens are obtained but never sent. Add token to all API calls: headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` }
CRITICAL: Backend must verify user_id ownership on every authed route. Ensure RLS context is set via withAuth on ALL protected handlers
CRITICAL: Recalculate payment amounts server-side. Never trust client-provided documentType or amount. Fetch document, verify user owns it, recalculate price from PRICING_CONFIG
HIGH: Secure error logging - do not send full stack traces to external services. Filter sensitive data in ErrorBoundary
HIGH: Backend must validate file uploads (size, MIME type, magic bytes). Never trust client-side validation alone
HIGH: Add server-side TOS verification - don't rely on client-side localStorage cache for sensitive acceptance checks
MEDIUM: If TERMS_OF_SERVICE becomes dynamic, sanitize markdown with DOMPurify and restrict HTML rendering
MEDIUM: Sanitize user form inputs (firstName, lastName, etc.) with Zod or DOMPurify before storing in state
MEDIUM: Remove skipPayment development bypass from GenerateButton.js - use staging environment for testing instead
LOW: Run 'npm audit' and update dependencies, particularly react-markdown and @auth0/nextjs-auth0
LOW: Verify CSP headers in next.config.mjs are set correctly and CSP violations are logged
